### Historical audit — H0185

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_12/lanes/codex_parallel_12_lane3/codex_parallel_12_lane3_I_r1/infer_logs/kea-atomic-signal-selectors/turn_1/trajs.json` (all event references below are to this file).

| Question | Evidence and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Goal | The task identifier suggests work on Kea atomic signal selectors, but the actual task specification is not visible. The student's final message indicates it believed a `main` ref or permission to branch from HEAD was needed; the underlying instruction is not shown (main agent event 7, characters [0,703)). |
| Autonomous exploration | The student inspected the repository, Git status and branches, source directory, instruction-file names, and `package.json` (events 1–6, respectively characters [0,691), [0,1036), [0,716), [0,576), [0,542), [0,10868)). The results showed detached HEAD at `6c7ebba`, a named `master` branch, and no listed remote or `main` branch. Reading the package manifest exposed test scripts, but no test execution is visible. |
| Changes and outcome | No edit or implementation appears in the trace. Inventory metadata reports a zero-byte patch and **empty patch, formally not solved**: 0/12 fail-to-pass and 139/139 pass-to-pass tests. These are reported evaluation results, not evidence of a partially correct implementation. The student stopped and requested a `main` ref or authorization to use HEAD (event 7). The trajectory metadata records normal completion and `end_turn`, not a technical interruption (top-level metadata, characters [0,4709)). |
| Teacher input | Hint and review paths are listed as available in the supplied inventory, but their contents and a captured delivery are not shown. The trajectory metadata reports zero teacher checks and zero teacher wait time (top-level metadata, characters [0,4709)). Thus no actual teacher input or adoption is evidenced; a later review cannot be assumed to have influenced this round. |

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, checking repository state before changing it can expose a workflow ambiguity, and asking for clarification avoids assuming an unapproved base. Here, the missing `main` ref was the student's stated blocker, not an independently established reason that the task could not be completed. Whether the original instructions required that branch, whether a valid alternative was available, and what selector behavior was required remain unresolved. No algorithm was implemented, so this record does not establish an algorithmic failure.
